rv.q: Jessica Lazar's production of Anthony E Palermo's intimate adaptation, styled as a 1940s live radio play, provides a resounding answer: yes! Do bother!

It's a question I often wonder, and one that It's a Wonderful Life faces on two counts. Not only is Franz Capra's life-affirming 1946 drama beloved and revered, but it's also a Christmas film. People don't just know and love it, but return time and time again, the actors' faces indelibly buffered into our minds with every yearly rewatch.
